newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish BDM brokerage plans closed-end fund.
newsitem.headline: Polish BDM brokerage plans closed-end fund.

text.p: Polish brokerage Beskidzki Dom Maklerski SA (BDM) plans to launch a closed-end fund as early as the end of next year's first quarter, the brokerage's president said on Thursday.
"We're hoping the closed-end fund will be formed by the end of the the first quarter next year and that turnover in units could start soon thereafter," Boguslaw Holeksa told Reuters.
He said the fund would have a start-up capital of up to 10 million zlotys and that an open-end and pension fund could be added by mid-1997.

He said the closed-end fund would invest in firms approved for public trade but not yet on the bourse and firms in Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) mass privatisation programme as well as in listed companies.

Under the NFI scheme each of Poland's 28 million adults can buy one NFI unit and later exchange it for shares in each of 15 funds which are run by domestic and foreign management firms and group more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation.
Holeksa said BDM expected by the end of next year to be the market maker of 10 to 20 NFI firms which plan to be listed on Poland's nascent over-the-counter market due to start trade later this month.

He said BDM would hold 25 to 30 percent of the shares in the mutual fund company, followed by minority BDM shareholders Stalexport, the Huta Katowice steel mill and 25 to 30 firms in Poland's NFI programme.
